title: Browsing the Aisles or Browsing the App? How Online Grocery Shopping is Changing What We Buy
authors: Sai Chand Chintala; Jūra Liaukonytė; Nathan Yang
eligible_reason: Compares Instacart (online) and brick-and-mortar baskets within household: trip-level outcomes regressed on a trip-level instacart indicator with user-by-time and user-by-retailer-by-quarter FE. The indicator marks the channel of each trip, not an absorbing household adoption; no staggered DiD or event study.
design_notes: Section3_Table4.R, Section4_Figure5.R, Section4_Table7.R, Section4_Table8.R: feols(log outcome ~ instacart | USER_ID^RETAILER^Year_Quarter + USER_ID^Year_Month, cluster USER_ID^RETAILER) on characteristic (routine) trips. No adoption timing variable in the code.
data_files_note: README: Numerator data under NDA; shipped files are 'simulated data' from random 50% draws of the original with random noise added to each variable; results differ from the paper.
data_provenance_note: Random 50% draw with additive noise on every variable (fuzzed); excluded as synthetic/disguised under 5b.
screener_notes: No article text or published PDF available locally (data/text/mksc and papers/mksc checked Nov 2); screened from README, regression inventory, main-results code and OpenAlex abstract. Out of scope.
